svg.aria-label: Animated diagram of the memory hierarchy inside one langgraph-beads-memory session, in six parts. Scope: one session_id spans many LangGraph thread_ids; a root namespace belongs to the supervisor, and each forked sub-agent gets its own child namespace named by a random hash suffix, with namespace ids otherwise derived deterministically from session_id and extra_path; sub-agents read their own namespace plus their ancestors, never a sibling's. Anatomy: a single fact card exploded to show its kind, status, source, body, embedding, and content-addressed short id, derived from session, namespace, source, and body hash. Kinds: a user message splits into one fact per claim; user_input, conclusion, and summary facts are retrievable by default, while directive facts -- questions, instructions, or goals -- are captured and queryable but held out of default retrieval so they don't crowd out real constraints. Lifecycle: active facts are retrievable; a supersedes edge or compaction retires a fact to superseded or archived, excluded from retrieval but kept for audit -- nothing is ever deleted. Edges: rollup_of links a summary fact back to every raw fact behind it for audit; a supersedes edge retires a stale fact but is guarded, refused unless the two facts are semantically close, cosine similarity at least 0.55; contradicts, relates_to, and derived_from are also part of the relation set. Retrieval: a query pulls its top-K matches from facts that are active, non-directive, and in the caller's own namespace or its ancestors, never a sibling's, and injects them with short ids the agent can cite.
svg.title: langgraph-beads-memory: the memory hierarchy inside one session
svg.text: langgraph-beads-memory — the memory hierarchy inside one session
Structure, not flow: what a memory consists of, where it lives, and what can retrieve it.

g.text: 1 · Scope hierarchy — one session, many namespaces
forked sub-agent — the hash suffix (sub-3f2a) is the one random part
reads: self + ancestors only — siblings never see each other
id = sha256(session_id, namespace_id, source, source_key, body)
— content-addressed; a checkpoint replay writes nothing new.
3 · Fact kinds — one claim per fact
retirement and deletion are different things
guarded: refused unless the two facts are
derived_from — compaction summary → what it replaced
injected into context, cited by short id
same rule applies inside a sub-agent — self + ancestors only
1 · Scope — one session_id spans many thread_ids. Root namespace is the supervisor's; each forked sub-agent gets its own child namespace with a random hash suffix.
2 · Anatomy — a fact carries kind, status, source, body, and an embedding; its id is content-addressed from session, namespace, source, and body.
3 · Kinds — a message splits into one fact per claim. Directives are captured but held out of default retrieval — they'd otherwise crowd out real constraints.
4 · Lifecycle — active facts are retrievable; supersedes or compaction retires a fact to superseded or archived. Nothing is ever deleted, only excluded.
5 · Edges — rollup_of links a summary back to every raw fact behind it; supersedes is guarded, refused unless the two facts are semantically close (cosine ≥ 0.55).
6 · Retrieval — top-K is drawn from facts that are active, non-directive, and in the caller's own namespace or its ancestors, never a sibling's.
The memory hierarchy inside one session: a session_id spanning many threads, forked
namespaces read by self+ancestors only, four fact kinds (directives held out of retrieval),
a lifecycle where nothing is deleted, typed edges, and retrieval scoped to active, in-scope facts.
